pylons_vi: 2 tháp chữ Y ngược hình đỉnh núi, cao 187 m: hai chân nhập thành một thân thon nhọn mũi, dưới mặt cầu là thân trụ đơn có khấc
pylons_en: 2 inverted-Y 'mountain peak' pylons, 187 m: legs merge into a tapered mast with a pointed spire; a single grooved stem below the deck

pylon_custom.description: Inverted Y ('mountain peak'): two legs straddle the deck just outside its edges and lean inward to merge ≈59 % of the above-deck height into one tall tapered mast that carries both stay planes on its faces and ends in a pointed obelisk spire. Just below the deck the legs turn inward through a solid 'cup' (chalice) under the girder and continue down as two closely spaced columns that read as a single grooved stem to the water.

model3d.notes: Main bridge (40 + 40 + 150 + 550 + 150 + 40 + 40) m, L = 1,010 m (TEDI technical design); 550 m main span and 187 m pylons (press). Deck 21.0 m incl. 2 × 1.75 m stay-anchor strips; hybrid girder: PC box near the pylons / side spans, steel–concrete composite box in the central main span. Inverted-Y 'mountain peak' pylons per the official render (TEDI): legs merge at ≈59 % of the above-deck height into a tapered mast with an obelisk spire; below the deck a solid cup and a single grooved stem. Proportions from the near-elevation render (deck ≈0.30 of the water-to-tip height): deck 55 m above full-pool water, tip 132 m above the deck. Two fan planes from the mast faces; 22 stays per side per plane (count estimated). White pylons, light stays (red-orange stays in some aerial renders are an alternative scheme). Pylon foundations: 45 bored piles D2.2 m, ≈85 m, in > 40 m of water.
